key_insight: RAG configuration shaped T2DM phenotyping performance: general-purpose embeddings favored sensitivity, while biomedical embeddings and few-shot prompts favored specificity and PPV.
clinical_relevance: RAG may support EHR-based research cohort identification, with configurations selected to balance missed cases, false positives, and token use.
method: Processed 170,678 clinical notes from 275 ICD-screened patients using GPT-4o.
Benchmarked seven embedding models and 350 embedding–chunk size–retrieval depth combinations on training data.
Evaluated eight optimized configurations with three prompt strategies against ICD codes and PheNorm.
evidence_signal: Across 24 test-set prompt–configuration combinations, mean sensitivity was 0.902, specificity 0.791, and F1 0.920; all exceeded ICD-code PPV, and sensitivity was significantly higher than PheNorm.
watch_item: Results from a small, ICD-screened cohort may not generalize to unscreened populations or other diseases, and token use varied substantially by embedding model.
paper_title: Systematic Benchmarking and Optimization of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) for Clinical Phenotyping: A Type II Diabetes Case Study in an ICD-Screened Cohort
